quizzes.stem: A pipeline step runs `claude "Analyze this pull request"` and hangs. What fixes it?

options.a: Point its input at an empty file so it cannot wait
options.b: Export an environment variable that selects headless mode
options.c: Add a batch flag so the call is queued
options.d: Add the print flag so that the run answers and exits

explanation.d: `-p` is the documented way to run without a person.
explanation.b: Ruled out because no such variable exists: "There is no headless environment variable and no `--batch` flag on the command line".
explanation.c: is ruled out for the same reason: "There is no headless environment variable and no `--batch` flag on the command line".
explanation.a: Ruled out because it is a workaround: "Redirecting standard input from an empty file is a Unix workaround that does not change how Claude Code runs."

quizzes.stem: A pipeline has a gate that stops merges until it passes and a dependency digest that people read on Monday. Which calls move to batch?

options.a: Just the one nobody waits on, while the other stays in real time
options.b: Both of them, with polling to find out when the gate is ready
options.c: Neither of them, since the results of a batch arrive in any order
options.d: Both of them, with a fallback to real time when a batch is slow

explanation.a: Nobody waits for the digest and a developer waits for the gate.
explanation.b: Ruled out because waiting is the problem: "Polling a batch does not make it finish sooner."
explanation.c: Ruled out because matching exists: "Results of a batch come back matched by `custom_id`, so their order is no reason to avoid it."
explanation.d: Ruled out because it adds a path: "A fallback to real time when a batch is slow adds a second path and a second bill".

quizzes.stem: What bounds the number of steps of a run that nobody watches?

options.a: A longer timeout on the job that contains it
options.b: A prompt that asks it to finish as quickly as it can
options.c: A turn limit set in the command
options.d: Running it again whenever it fails to produce an answer

explanation.c: A limit set in the command stops the loop: "`--max-turns` stops a loop".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a sentence is no limit: "A prompt that asks the run to be quick is a request, not a limit."
explanation.a: Ruled out because time does not stop a loop: "A longer job timeout only lets a loop run longer."
explanation.d: Ruled out because repeating the run changes nothing: "re-running it repeats the cost with no reason to expect a different result".

quizzes.stem: A review of nine changed modules gives deep notes on some and shallow ones on others, and flags a pattern in one while approving it in another. How should it be restructured?

options.a: A model with a larger context window, for the same single pass
options.b: A pass for each file, then one pass on how the files fit together
options.c: Three full runs, keeping only the issues that two of them report
options.d: A rule that pull requests may not change more than four files

explanation.b: Dividing the work answers the cause, thinning attention.
explanation.a: Ruled out because room is not attention: "A larger context window does not fix attention quality."
explanation.c: Ruled out because agreement hides rare finds: "Keeping only the issues that two of three runs agree on would hide real bugs that are found only now and then."
explanation.d: Ruled out because it shifts the work: "Asking authors to split their pull requests moves the work to people and does not improve the review."

quizzes.stem: Which `passes` setting does the practice's review case accept?

explanation.d: A pass for each file, then the integration pass.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the order matters: "`passes` is `per-file` and then `integration`, in that order".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the second pass is not an integration pass: "`passes` is `per-file` and then `integration`, in that order".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the first pass is not per file: "`passes` is `per-file` and then `integration`, in that order".

quizzes.stem: Which command does the practice's commands case accept?

explanation.b: The flag, the JSON format and the turn limit are all present.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the print flag is missing: "has `-p` or `--print`, `--output-format json` and `--max-turns` with a number".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the JSON format is missing: "has `-p` or `--print`, `--output-format json` and `--max-turns` with a number".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the turn limit is missing: "has `-p` or `--print`, `--output-format json` and `--max-turns` with a number".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5, a pipeline that reviews pull requests and writes tests. A job must decide whether to fail, but the seriousness of each comment is free text. What fixes that?

options.a: Ask the model to put the word critical at the very start of any serious comment it makes
options.b: Ask for JSON that follows a schema where severity is one of a few fixed values
options.c: Count the comments and fail the job once they pass a fixed number chosen by the team
options.d: Search the prose of every comment for the words that usually go with a bad finding

explanation.b: A closed list can be compared with a floor.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a word in prose is a convention: "A sentence that asks for more care is a request; the criteria are the case list."
explanation.c: Ruled out because a count says nothing about how bad a finding is: "what each severity means, with one example for each".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the severity belongs in the schema: "The severity then belongs in the schema as a closed list, so a script can compare it with a floor."

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5, a pipeline that reviews pull requests and writes tests. The job script ignores how the command ended, and the job is green although the run stopped at its turn limit. What is the remedy?

options.a: Read the exit status and the JSON, and fail whenever no valid answer exists
options.b: Raise the turn limit until the run always finishes well before it reaches that limit
options.c: Run the command again whenever the output that comes back looks a little too short
options.d: Remove the turn limit so that a run stops only when all of its work is finished

explanation.a: The gate fails the job whenever no valid answer exists.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the limit exists to stop a loop: "`--max-turns` stops a loop".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a rerun changes nothing: "re-running it repeats the cost with no reason to expect a different result".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the limit is what ends the run by itself: "A run with no person must end by itself".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5, a pipeline that reviews pull requests and writes tests. The audit of the draft prints `batchable: debt-report`. What does that finding report?

options.a: A scheduled job runs in real time and pays full price
options.b: A job that someone waits for runs as a batch
options.c: A command that starts claude lacks the print flag
options.d: A review is made in one pass and in a shared session

explanation.a: The finding is about a scheduled job: "`batchable`: a scheduled job that runs in real time and pays full price."
explanation.b: Ruled out because that is the other finding: "`blocking-batch`: a job someone waits for that runs as a batch."
explanation.c: Ruled out because that is a third: "`no-print-flag`: a command that starts `claude` without `-p` or `--print`."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the design of a review has its own findings: "`single-pass-review`, `shared-session`, `no-prior-findings` and `writes`: the design of a review".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S5, a pipeline that reviews pull requests and writes tests. The job that only looks at code has been given the right to run whatever it likes on the machine. What is the problem?

options.a: Shell access output is not valid JSON, so the schema of the answer cannot be applied to it
options.b: Shell access slows every run down, and a turn limit would then end that run far too soon
options.c: Shell access changes things, so the list should hold reading and searching tools only
options.d: Shell access needs a person to approve each call, and nobody is there to give that approval

explanation.c: A review changes nothing, so it needs only reading tools.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the issue is what the tool can do: "A shell tool is a way to change things".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the schema applies to the answer and not to the commands: "The severity then belongs in the schema as a closed list".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the command's approval is listed in advance: "`--allowedTools` lists what runs without asking, because nobody can approve a prompt".
